vertical file list, ~97px (~40-48pt) row pitch, [system icon]+[filename] on shared axis, gray Title-Case section header above rows, top row pre-selected; neutral inset-rounded selection fill (~6-8pt), white text, NO accent tint

signature_moves: Accent suppression / the neutral stage: selection is a low-contrast NEUTRAL gray inset-rounded fill with white (not accent-tinted) text; no focus ring, no primary-action colour, no accent anywhere in chrome — the launcher stays chromatically silent so content carries all colour (deliberate inverse of native accent-tinted selection; costs selection contrast)

Palette-as-stage grammar: no window at all — full-bleed near-black translucent HUD, search text with no field chrome, generous ~40-48pt rows; the ⌘K command-palette design language (peers Spotlight/Alfred/Linear command menu) at HUD scale

Master-detail inside the palette: a two-pane list+inspector (35/65) living inside the floating launcher — the command palette becomes a mini file browser with metadata inspector without ever growing window chrome
defects: Weak focus/selection appearance (WCAG 2.4.13) / Contrast Dilution — selection fill ~1.3-1.5:1 above bg and no accent tint/ring/weight change, so the only cue for the keyboard-driven selection is a barely-there fill; canon would add a >=3:1 shift
Faint split divider — 1pt list/inspector divider ~<3:1 (lum ~30 on ~8), near-invisible

aesthetic.direction: Neo-grotesque product (dark-neutral ramp, Linear/Vercel family) rendered native in SF Pro — restrained/accent-suppressed colour strategy; the one brand colour (red) is reserved for marketing, never the UI chrome

psychology: Hick's Law — collapses 'everything you can do' into one search box + a short ranked list; decision time becomes typing, not scanning a menu
Jakob's Law — adopts the Spotlight/⌘K convention users already know; conventional interface, innovative product
Von Restorff / accent discipline — suppressing accent everywhere removes false emphasis so content previews pop by contrast alone; double-edged, it also weakens the selection signal (the #14 finding)
Serial-position + goal-gradient — top result pre-selected ('the top hit is usually right'), so Enter resolves the task with zero further aiming
Aesthetic-usability effect — cinematic dark polish buys first-contact trust for a utility
Fitts's Law — full-width ~97px rows are effectively giant targets (though the surface is keyboard-first)
